body.p: Claims 1-24 are pending in this application. By this Amendment, specification and claims 1-20 are amended, and claims 21-24 are added. Support for the amendments can be found in, for example, paragraphs [0014], [0016], and [0054]-[0059] and Figures 1, 3, and 6 of the application as originally filed. No new matter is added. Reconsideration and allowance in due course is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-20 are objected to due to informalities. It is respectfully submitted that the
body.h1: amendments to the claims filed herewith are responsive to the Examiner's comments, and thus
body.p: the objection to the claims should be withdrawn.
Claims 1-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly indefinite. It is

respectfully submitted that the amendments to the claims are responsive to the examiner's comments, and that claims 1-20 meet the requirements of 35 U.S.C. § 112(b). Accordingly, thisrejection should be withdrawn.
Claim 13 is not otherwise rejected over art. It is thus assumed, for purposes of this response, that claim 13 defines patentable subject matter.
Claims 1, 4-8, 11, and 12 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as allegedly anticipated by Chribkow et al. (EP 1944234, hereinafter "Chribkow"). This rejection is respectfully traversed.

Chribkow does not disclose or suggest all of the features recited in independent claim 1, or the claimed combination of features. For example, as discussed during the interview, Chribkow does not disclose or suggest An aircraft, including, inter alia, "a plurality of vertical lift propulsor assemblies, each of the plurality of vertical lift propulsor assemblies including a propulsor coupled to the aircraft and driven by an electric motor including a rotor and a stator; and a cyclic control assembly," as recited in independent

claim 1, nort that the cyclic control assembly includes " an actuator; and a push rod extending through a shaft coupling the rotor to the propulsor, wherein the push rod is coupled to the actuator and the propulsor; the push rod is configured to increase a blade angle of the propulsor in response to a displacement of the push rod in a first direction; and the push rod is configured to decrease the blade angle of the propulsor in response to a displacement of the push rod in a second direction," as recited in independent claim 1.

For at least these reasons, it is respectfully submitted that independent claim 1 is not anticipated by Chribkow, and thus the rejection of independent claim 1 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) over Chribkow should be withdrawn. Dependent claims 4-8, 11, and 12 are allowable at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which they depend, as well as for their additional features.

Claims 2, 3, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly unpatentable over Chribkow. It appears, based on the Examiner's comments following this statement of rejection in the Office Action, that it was the Examiner's intention to include claim 9 in this rejection. This rejections, insofar as it applies to claims 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20, is respectfully traversed.

Dependent claims 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20 are allowable over Chribkow at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which they depend, as well as for their additional features. It is respectfully submitted that it would not have been obvious to modify the rotor system disclosed by Chribkow in the manner suggested in the Office Action, to incorporate the features of claims 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20.

It is respectfully submitted the Official Notice is liberally applied to a large number of claims/features, relying on a generalized statement without any documentary evidence for support. . Should the Examiner maintain the rejection after considering the reasoning presented herein, Applicant submits that the Examiner must provide "the explicit basis on which the examiner regards the matter as subject to official notice and allow the applicant to challenge the assertion in the next reply after the Office action in which the 'common knowledge' statement was made," or else withdraw the rejection. See, MPEP § 2144.03.

For at least these reasons, it is respectfully submitted that dependent claims 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20 are allowable, and thus the rejection of claims 2, 3, 9, 10, 11, 14-18, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) over Chribkow should be withdrawn.
Claim 19 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103(a) as allegedly unpatentable over Chribkow in view of Rehm (U.S. 5,826,822, hereinafter "Rehm"). This rejection is respectfully traversed.

Dependent claim 19 is allowable over Chribkow at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which it depends, as well as for its additional features, and Rehm fails to overcome the deficiencies of Chribkow. Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that claim 19 is allowable over the applied combination, and thus this rejection should
be withdrawn

New claims 21-24 are added to the application. It is respectfully submitted that new dependent claims 21-24 are allowable at least for the reasons set forth above with respect to independent claim 1, from which they depend, as well as for their additional features.

It is respectfully submitted that the claims are in condition for allowance and notification to that effect is earnestly requested. The Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned to facilitate prosecution of this application.

It is believed that all of the rejections have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Finally, nothing in this document should be construed as intended to concede any issue with regard to any claim, except as specifically stated in this document, and the amendment of any claim does not necessarily signify concession of unpatentability of the claim prior to its amendment.
